objective: Extend FAISAL with a provider-neutral deterministic sandbox-execution contract informed by Firecracker, Wasmtime, and paid-provider background execution semantics.

findings: Zircon uses explicit kernel object and job/process ownership concepts; FAISAL can adopt explicit parentage and authority boundaries without replacing Linux.

Firecracker is a user-space KVM VMM with minimal devices, API-controlled microVM lifecycle, resource rate limiters, metadata service, and jailer isolation; it is a backend, not a Linux kernel replacement.

Wasmtime/WebAssembly uses explicit imports/exports, bounds-checked memory, type-checked control flow, no raw system calls, and capability-based WASI filesystem access; interruption and deterministic execution are available with tradeoffs.
OpenAI background mode provides asynchronous provider-side polling, cancellation, and stream cursor resumption; FAISAL must persist provider handles and cursors independently for durable objectives.
AIOS/vLLM/model-provider APIs remain user-space model/agent systems. FAISAL’s role is to enforce resource, authority, lineage, recovery, and evidence boundaries around them.

features: generation fencing for stale sandbox state
CPU, memory, I/O, and fuel budgets
provider handle and stream cursor binding
monotonic sequence and nonce replay protection
start, fuel consumption, checkpoint, resume, cancel, and completion state machine
authorized completion and result digest requirements
fail-closed resource, deadline, authority, tamper, and cancellation behavior

benchmark.scope: local userspace policy fixture, not Wasm execution, Firecracker boot, KVM, or provider latency

known_boundary.acpi_on_two_vcpu: known rcu_preempt stall profile remains rejected by existing hardened runner
known_boundary.interpretation: The M228 contract is a userspace policy/state-machine fixture; it does not qualify Wasmtime, Firecracker, KVM, physical sandboxing, or vendor infrastructure.

comparison.faisal_advantage: agent/objective/tenant lineage, authority, generation fencing, deterministic budgets, fuel/deadline/cancellation, checkpoint digest binding, and durable provider-cursor boundary
comparison.firecracker_advantage: real KVM microVM isolation, device model, VMM, jailer, and hardware virtualization
comparison.wasmtime_advantage: real Wasm execution, linear-memory sandbox, imports/exports, WASI implementation, and runtime-specific interruption/determinism
comparison.paid_provider_advantage: real asynchronous model execution and provider-managed state/availability

boundary.fast_boot_claim: qualified only for the existing ACPI-off one-vCPU QEMU profile
boundary.note: No physical backend, external reviewer, provider service, production signing ceremony, or production approval was fabricated.
